fields.h1: Build a Creative Request Form That Hands Designers a Full Brief
fields.hero_description: Get a creative request form that asks each deliverable's specs up front and saves every request to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Designer Needs Before the First Draft
fields.features_subheading: Designers start from a complete brief instead of a chat thread. Each request keeps its specs and reference files in one place.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the deliverable

A requester picks print, digital ad, video, or copy first. The form then asks only what that piece needs, such as trim size and quantity for print or running time for video.
fields.feature_2:
A lead time the form holds to

Set how much notice you need before work starts. A due date inside that window marks the request as a rush, and the requester has to give a reason before it can be sent.
fields.feature_3:
Brand files attached at the start

Requesters upload the logo and any reference pieces with the request. Designers open one record that holds everything, instead of asking for the logo again by email.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts when a request changes hands

The app posts in Slack or sends an email when a request is assigned to a designer or ready for review. A reminder goes out when feedback has waited past the date you set.
fields.feature_5:
Requests you can search later

Each request saves as a row in a database you own, with no response caps. Filter by department or deliverable type to see which groups asked for what work last quarter.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

On paid plans, export the full code of your creative request app to your GitHub repository. Connect it to the project tool you already use for design work through its API.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Requests, Each Ready for a Designer
fields.tab_content_1:
Due in 6 days when the team needs 10, the poster is a rush

Vintercroft Community College's events office orders its posters through the marketing team. Gwenllian Arbuckle asked for 60 jazz night posters at 11 x 17 in., due in 6 business days. The team needs 10, and the form marked her request as a rush. It would not send until she gave a reason: the venue was confirmed late.
fields.tab_content_2:
From 3 placements, 6 files with their sizes

Kaveh Delgadillo plans the fall boot sale ads at Haverstock Outfitters. He ticked 3 placements on the form, and it filled in each size: 1080 x 1080 for the feed, 1080 x 1920 for stories, and 1200 x 628 for link ads. With 2 headline versions per placement, the designer got a list of 6 files to make.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any round past two waits for the director's yes

Aino Mirembe ordered a 30-second auto loan video for the lobby screens at Solvay Ridge Credit Union. Her request came with 2 revision rounds, and she used both on the voiceover and the end card. When she asked for round 3, it went to creative director Iskander Hjelm to approve before the editor opened the file again.
fields.tab_content_4:
Even at 6 each after two requests move

Fiammetta Aguilera runs the in-house creative team at Tilbury Freight. Her queue showed 18 open requests: 8 with Maks, 6 with Ulla, and 4 with Oskari. She moved 2 of Maks's requests to Oskari, and the app emailed him both briefs. Each designer now has 6.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Creative Request Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up a creative request form that asks the right questions for each piece and keeps rush work on record.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the lead time for each kind of work
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for the files the designer will need
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the pieces people ask your designers for, such as event posters or social ads. Each one becomes a choice at the top of the form, and that choice decides which questions come next.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for trim size and quantity on print, and running time and where it will play on video. Keep each set short. A requester answers only the questions for the piece they picked.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick the notice each deliverable needs, such as 10 business days for print and 15 for video. Name the one person who can accept a rush, and put the earliest allowed due date next to the date field.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add an upload for the logo, the final copy, and any examples the requester likes. Require the copy on pieces that cannot start without it. A designer who has the final words lays the piece out once, around text that will not change.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the number of rounds a request includes, such as 2, and who approves one more. State it on the form above the send button, where requesters read it before they commit to a due date.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Describe it to Emergent and test it
fields.howto_step_6_des: Paste your deliverables and their lead times into a prompt, and Emergent builds the form and its database. Send a test request for a poster due tomorrow, and check that it is marked as a rush.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Open the form to every team
fields.howto_step_7_des: Share one link with every department that asks for creative work, and stop taking requests by email. Check the queue each Monday and move work between designers before anyone falls behind.

faq_plan.q: What is a creative request form?
faq_plan.a: A creative request form is the brief a person fills in to ask a design or marketing team for new work, such as a poster or a video. It records what the piece is for, the specs, the files to use, and the due date. The team starts from that record instead of a thread of follow-up questions.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a creative request form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: the pieces your designers make, the questions each one needs, and the notice you ask for. Emergent builds the form and a database for the requests, and you change either one by prompting again. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a creative request form ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with who is asking and what they need, then the purpose of the piece and who it is for. Add the specs, such as size or running time, along with the due date and where the piece will run. Close with an upload for the logo and copy, plus a box for anything the designer should avoid.

faq_plan.q: Should a creative request form ask for a budget?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the work costs money outside the team, such as printing, stock photos, or paid ad spend. Ask for the amount and who approves it. If that money is not set aside yet, the requester gets it approved first through a budget request form and attaches the approval to the creative request.

faq_plan.q: How much notice should a creative request form require?
faq_plan.a: Set the notice by kind of work, not one number for everything. Take the last 20 jobs of each kind, measure the days from request to delivery, and set the lead time a few days above the median. Revisit it each quarter, since a new designer or a new printer changes the numbers.

faq_plan.q: How should a creative request form handle rush requests?
faq_plan.a: Let a rush through, but make it visible. Require a reason, send the rush to one named person to accept or decline, and show the requester which queued work moves back if it is accepted. Count rushes by department each quarter: a team that sends one every week needs an earlier planning date.

faq_plan.q: When does a creative request form need a kickoff meeting?
faq_plan.a: It needs one when the work is large or the request leaves open questions, such as a campaign with several pieces or a video with a shoot. Add a question asking whether the requester wants a kickoff, and let them book a time through a meeting request form. A resized ad can go straight to a designer.

faq_plan.q: How many revision rounds should a creative request form include?
faq_plan.a: Start with 2: one round for larger changes and one for final fixes. Write the number on the form, and send any extra round to the person who plans the team's time. In the app Emergent builds, each round saves to the request in a database you own, and you can see which departments ask for extra rounds.

faq_plan.q: Can one creative request form cover print, video, and social work?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for the type of work first and show each type only its own questions, which keeps paper stock off a video request. Every type then lands in one list sorted by due date. Emergent builds that branching from a sentence in your prompt, and you add a new type later the same way.

faq_plan.q: What should a creative request form ask before a photo or video shoot?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the date, the location, and who will be on camera, plus a short list of the shots the piece cannot go out without. Ask who on site can answer questions on the day. If the shoot needs cameras or lights the team borrows, the crew books them through an equipment request form.
